cases.question: How do I make Le Tourin garlic soup?

response.answer: Le Tourin is a garlic soup from the village of Le Fleix in Dordogne, served for 2 with a total time of 30 minutes. Brown the chopped garlic in olive oil in a frying pan, add the flour and cook a few minutes to remove the floury taste, then gradually stir in the water and cook for 10 minutes. Beat the egg white, temper it with a ladleful of soup and stir it back into the pot. Combine the egg yolk, pepper and vinegar, temper the yolks with a ladleful of soup, then remove the soup from the heat, stir in the yolk mixture and season with salt. Place thin slices of bread in each bowl, pour the soup on top and serve hot. The recipe notes that you can optionally use an equal mixture of chopped onions and garlic. Ingredients: 10 to 12 cloves garlic chopped, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 tablespoon flour, 4 cups water or as needed, 1 egg separated, pepper to taste, 1 teaspoon vinegar, salt to taste. Steps: 1. In a frying pan, brown the chopped garlic (10–12 cloves) in 1 tablespoon olive oil. 2. Add 1 tablespoon flour, mix well, and cook a few minutes to remove the floury taste. 3. Gradually stir in 4 cups water, or as needed, and cook for 10 minutes. 4. Beat the egg white in a small bowl, gradually whisk in a ladleful of soup, then stir the mixture back into the pot. 5. Combine the egg yolk, pepper and 1 teaspoon vinegar in a small bowl, temper the yolks with a ladleful of soup. 6. Remove the soup from the heat, stir in the yolk mixture, and season with salt to taste. 7. Place thin slices of bread in each bowl, pour the soup on top, and serve hot. cases.question: How do I make a sweet mango yogurt drink?

Mix sugar with the mango nectar until dissolved. 2. Gradually add the milk to the yoghurt. 3. Mix together the mango and yoghurt mixtures. cases.question: What's the method for pasta carbonara?

response.answer: The first recipe, Spaghetti alla Carbonara, makes it as follows. Dice the guanciale or pancetta into 2.5 cm pieces and bring a big pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the spaghetti until al dente, drain it and reserve 1 cup of the water. Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the pork and cook about 10 minutes over low heat until most of the fat has rendered but it is still chewy and barely browned. In a bowl, slowly whisk about ½ cup of the pasta water into the 5 egg yolks, then add the grated Pecorino Romano and Parmigiano-Reggiano and mix well with a fork. Transfer the spaghetti straight to the skillet, toss and turn off the heat. Add the egg and cheese mixture, stirring in the remaining pasta water to thin the sauce and form an emulsion. Add the pepper and toss to coat. Another version, Carbonara Pasta, uses 4 eggs, cubed pancetta, thyme, onion and lemon zest and is cooled before being mixed with the yolks off the heat. The ingredient list comes from the source page and may be incomplete.

The first recipe, Spaghetti alla Carbonara, makes it as follows. Dice 225–500 g guanciale or pancetta into 2.5 cm pieces. Bring a big pot of water to a boil and salt it when it begins to simmer. Cook 450 g spaghetti until al dente, drain it and reserve 1 cup of the water. While the pasta cooks, heat 3–4 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the pork and cook about 10 minutes over low heat until most of the fat has rendered but it is still chewy and barely browned. In a bowl, slowly whisk about ½ cup of the pasta water into 5 egg yolks, then add ¾ cup grated Pecorino Romano and ¾ cup grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and mix thoroughly with a fork. Transfer the drained spaghetti immediately to the skillet, toss and turn off the heat. Add the egg and cheese mixture while stirring in the remaining pasta water to thin the sauce and create an emulsion. Add ½ tablespoon freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. A variant, Carbonara Pasta, uses 4 eggs, 3 oz fresh pancetta, thyme, onion and lemon zest, and combines cooled fried pancetta with the raw yolks and hot drained pasta in a bowl instead of a skillet.
